Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Right knee pain associated with increased running for marathon training; onset ~2 weeks ago.
  - Pain begins after ~20 minutes of running; last run required stopping due to worsening pain.
  - Reports clicking during certain gym exercises (knee flexion/extension). Initially stated “knees” hurt and click; later clarified pain is in right knee only (conflict noted).
  - One episode of transient tingling in right toes after a run; resolved; no ongoing numbness/tingling.
  - Early episode of mild swelling after first run improved with ice; currently no swelling, redness, or heat.
  - No knee locking, giving way, instability, difficulty on stairs, or limitations in walking; able to fully flex and extend the knee.
  - No calf pain; no color or temperature change in lower leg.
  - Noted occasional sock indentation at ankles after prolonged standing.
  - Past issues: farsighted; history of LASIK surgery. Prior severe UTI (ER visit; kidney stones considered). No asthma, indigestion, or reflux reported.

Management Plan

- Continue ice therapy regularly to aid recovery.
- Reduce running volume/intensity; avoid running through pain.
- Physiotherapy referral placed for comprehensive knee assessment and management.
- Imaging (e.g., to assess cartilage/ligaments) to be considered based on physiotherapy assessment and clinical findings.
- Prescription: stronger anti-inflammatory to be taken regularly with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen. Sent to patient’s pharmacy.
- Red flags discussed: seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.
